scope: Nine manually composed paired-source development answers. Not automatic contradiction resolution, exhaustive chronology, audio verification or archive-wide latest-state certification.

cases.question: Did Johnny ever get past the Last of Us II bug?
cases.answer: Yes. CQ201 reports a ladder bug blocking Johnny near the end. CQ202 still reports no play and an unanswered support ticket. CQ203 explicitly reports that the bug was patched and he finished the game. These establish successive episode reports, not an exact patch date, technical cause or verified support response.
cases.reason: Coordinator checked all three source windows directly; the later explicit completion supersedes the open loop without inventing intermediate events.

cases.question: Did Dan Gomez lack Trespasser, or did he buy it between episodes?
cases.answer: CQ202 says Dan apparently wants Trespasser and lacks it. CQ203 explicitly corrects that claim: Dan has a copy, whose sticker advertises a soundtrack, unlike Tyler's copy. This is a correction to reported ownership, not evidence of a new purchase between episodes; the actual soundtrack's contents and format remain unknown.
cases.reason: The first claim is explicitly tentative, while the later erratum supplies ownership and a sticker comparison. Neither source dates an acquisition.

cases.question: Did Johnny resolve the missing Monster in My Pocket figurine?
cases.answer: Not in these passages. CQ76 introduces the included figurine and Johnny realizes he did not know about it. CQ78 says he checked his box after that episode and the figure was not there. A roughly $100 listing is discussed, but no purchase is reported. The later report confirms an unresolved completeness gap, not a completed acquisition.
cases.reason: CQ76 discovery and CQ78 explicit box check/listing are separate events; ownership of the game is not ownership of the figure.

cases.question: What happened to the promised Scooby-Doo microcast?
cases.answer: CQ76 promises a Scooby-Doo microcast the following week. CQ77 explains that it ran too long for that label and was published as a short regular episode, retaining references to the original format. Tyler's first intro there is not evidence that it was his first appearance. Omitting the usual buying segment does not prove the episode contains no purchase remarks.
cases.reason: Coordinator read full CQ76 and CQ77. Intro statements establish delivery with changed format, while the complete episode contains acquisition discussion despite no dedicated segment.

cases.question: Did Kat get Super Mario RPG back after listing it as a collection gap?
cases.answer: Yes, within these episode reports. CQ12 says she no longer has Super Mario RPG and wants selected SNES games back, not a complete set. CQ14 says she has it again for the third time and intends to keep it. The surrounding 'getting into' versus 'gonna get into' wording leaves the exact start of play ambiguous; it is not evidence of a completed playthrough or of reacquiring EarthBound and Chrono Trigger too.
cases.reason: Coordinator read both complete transcripts and the specific gap/reacquisition contexts. The later copy resolves only this named collection gap, with play uncertainty retained.

cases.question: Did Tyler finish the Saturn set he was close to completing?
cases.answer: CQ79 says he probably has three Saturn games left and specifically names All Star Baseball 97 as missing. CQ81 says Crypt Killer and All-Star Baseball 1997 were his last two and that the set is complete. These establish the reported goal changing to completion; they do not date every intervening purchase or prove Crypt Killer was the unnamed third game in CQ79.

cases.question: Had Kat played Super Mario Odyssey, or was that only Johnny's group summary?
cases.answer: In CQ80, the specific later statements that Kat has not played Odyssey qualify the loose group summary that everyone is playing it. By CQ81, Kat directly says she has played a little, mainly playing Mario Kart instead. Johnny's separate Europe completion belongs to him. This is a later reported change in Kat's play status, not a reason to rewrite CQ80 as already-played or to mark her finished.
cases.reason: Coordinator fully read both episodes; CQ81 peer independently confirmed its present-play and actor distinction. No exact first-play date is invented.
